Self.Wiki: An item pickup. When the map loads, the game reads the item lot and places its items as one pickup at the treasure part (a corpse, chest, item glow or other asset). The pickup glows and shows a prompt; taking it awards the lot and sets the lot's Get Item Flag, after which the pickup is not placed again. A treasure in a chest usually starts disabled and is switched on when the chest's ObjAct (on the same part) opens it.

TreasurePartName.Wiki: The part the pickup is placed at, normally an Asset or Dummy Asset (corpse, chest, item glow). The pickup takes this part's position unless an Action Button ID is set. In a chest, the chest's ObjAct must point at this same part. With no part, no pickup appears.

ItemLotID.Wiki: The ItemLotParam_map row to award. Every item in the row is given; following rows with consecutive IDs (lot + 1, + 2, ...) are given with it, so a pile of items uses a run of rows. The row's Get Item Flag records the pickup: once set, the treasure no longer appears. If the row doesn't exist, no pickup is placed.

ActionButtonID.Wiki: An ActionButtonParam row for the pickup prompt, or -1 for the default. When set, the pickup is placed at the action button's region (for example a dummy poly on the asset) instead of the part's origin, and it uses that row's text and range. Retail uses it for coffins, carriage chests, item glows and statues that giant enemies can break.

PickupAnimID.Wiki: The player animation played when taking the pickup, or -1 for the normal pickup animation. Retail uses 60070 for carriage chests and 7520 for some chests.

InChest.Wiki: What holds the pickup. Corpse or Loose (0) is the normal item on a corpse or the ground. Chest (1) is for items inside a chest; these are usually Start Disabled so the chest's ObjAct can reveal them. Item Glow (2) is for items shown by a separate glow asset, such as in pots, statues or event items. The names follow retail use; the exact difference in game behaviour is not confirmed.

StartDisabled.Wiki: If ON, the pickup is placed but hidden and can't be taken until something enables it. Opening the chest's ObjAct on the same part enables it, which is why most chest treasures use this. Turn it off for items that should be available at once.
